- Asset: https://polyhaven.com/a/boulder_01
- License: CC0 1.0; https://polyhaven.com/license and https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/
- Retrieved: 14 November 2026. Original glTF and 1K diffuse, packed AO/roughness/metallic, and OpenGL normal textures are retained here.
- Exact download URLs and upstream MD5 checksums: `files.json`. Downloaded dependencies matched their published MD5 values.
- Original glTF SHA256: `51487934db898b4c24072780a451e34eca5c02e3ada24a62bbc600bbc4019e92`.
- Runtime export: `game/public/assets/rocks/boulder-01-preview/boulder-01.glb`, 2,879,052 bytes; SHA256 `c539a3a38c54e8ee6a0ae7c10e3aca67db7185a32dfc33866bb0f02b5855408f`.
- Blender 4.2: weld coincident imported vertices at 0.00001 m, decimate the supplied 66,122-triangle glTF to 1,200 triangles, preserve UVs, normals and 1K maps, export GLB. This measured input count differs from the site's higher-resolution listing. Script retained beside this record.
- Runtime uses uniform scaling, partial burial, warm material tint and reduced normal/AO strengths. This is an Earth rock scan used as a visual candidate, not NASA terrain data or a scientifically identified Martian outcrop. The source includes mineral/lichen coloration; its final Mars material treatment needs visual approval.
- Only the first present-day hub shelf is replaced for review. The other shelves and episode remain on their baseline.

## Shared-surface runtime variant

The present-day hub now loads `boulder-01-shape.glb` (47,916 bytes), generated by `strip_runtime_materials.py`. All geometry buffer views are byte-identical to the 1,200-triangle textured candidate; only unused texture/material payloads are omitted. SHA256: `3c861ef2be8ac975f1bbbea401e734c42d7695aece3b5585d1792f84d1c9dead`. The original scan and textured candidate remain preserved.

The hub supplies the existing world-space rock material to this mesh, the five retained shelves and instanced rubble. This replaces the imported scan's dark multicolored surface with one coherent rock palette. Neutral vertex colors are supplied for the scan because the shared material expects them. Imported replacement materials are disposed; the shared rock material remains scene-owned and is disposed once with the scene.

## Six-site rock kit

The user subsequently authorized the full rollout. `prepare_hub_kit.py` derives four distinct fracture-cut shapes from this preserved scan. Runtime manifest and full provenance are in `game/public/assets/rocks/hub-kit-v1/`. The scene uses three principal silhouettes at six existing sites and eight relocated fragments, all with the established shared rock material. See `outputs/review/rock-rollout/REVIEW.md`.
